name: 19-ir-ratio-lit-room
incident: 2026-08-17 22:17:29 - an outbuilding light, measured; the case an absolute threshold gets wrong
description:
The acceptance test for the silent probe. A lit outbuilding: the night pipeline sits at 12160 and falls to 3226 when the light comes on, and the DAY pipeline then reads ~3700 - far above any workable absolute day threshold. Scenario 16 is the negative control: the same measured event WITHOUT the third curve, where staying night is the only verdict the evidence supports.

The third curve is what settles it. With the light on, killing the illuminator barely changes anything (3226 -> 3550, r = 1.10): the room supplies the light. In genuine darkness beforehand, killing it collapses the scene (12160 -> 45000, r = 3.7): the illuminator was doing the work. Same camera, same thresholds, opposite verdicts - and no absolute level was consulted.

Budgets are split on purpose: silent probes are cheap and several are fine, audible switches are not. Two switches is the whole budget - one into day when the light comes on, one back when it goes off.

EXTENDED 2026-08-22 (boot measures before it decides). Boot no longer takes the silent route - at t=0 nothing has established that our own illuminator is on, so the ratio has no premise - which means the boot pair is audible (budget 2 -> 4, both drives inside the first 15 s) and, more importantly, the r=3.7 darkness verdict this scenario asserts is no longer produced AT boot. The run therefore goes on to t=780 so the heartbeat probe after the light goes off at t=355 supplies it instead. That is the same measurement on the same curve at the other end of the run, not a weaker one: the two verdicts this scenario is named for - 'the illuminator carries this scene' in genuine darkness and 'the room supplies the light' with the light on - are both still asserted, from the same camera and the same thresholds.
